reasoning: Both attempts keep behavior identical, split the mixed table, remove the global fmt, and pass all three tools. Both also make the same mistake: getTallest keeps a bare return, which they document as intentional. A wins narrowly. It is shorter and easier to scan, it moves the score and variety logic into named helpers, and it names the returned table Module as the convention requires. B's documentation and its Counts type are slightly better, but B breaks the naming convention and is wordier.

criteria.note: The Lune parity check passes. isTallestCandidateType keeps getTallest accepting numeric Type indexes, the discount still starts above 50 blocks, and the format strings match the original exactly.

Names are spelled out, continue guard clauses replace the nested ifs, and the magic numbers are named constants. calculateScore and countBlockTypesUsed make summarize short. The filter is still written twice because of the legacy numeric-index quirk.
The local formatWholeNumber replaces the global fmt(n, c, d), and the one-decimal case uses string.format inline, so no call passes positional booleans.
The mixed table becomes a BLOCK_TYPES list of records plus a derived COST_BY_TYPE map.

The file passes --!strict and declares Block and Summary types, with the price map typed as number?. Counts is typed { [string]: number? }, which is slightly loose. getTallest still ends with a bare return, which the rubric asks to remove.
Only PlotStats.luau changes, the comments are accurate, all three tools pass, and the returned table is named Module.
The Lune parity check passes. isLegacyTypeIndex keeps getTallest's numeric-index behavior, assert and its message are kept, and the format strings match the original.

Names are clear, guard clauses replace the nested ifs, the constants are named, and section banners organize the file. It is verbose: the variety count and score are still inline in summarize, and the filter is only partly shared through getTypeCost.
formatWholeNumber, formatOneDecimal, addThousandsSeparators, and pluralize are all local functions with single purposes.
A typed BLOCK_TYPES list of BlockTypeInfo records plus a COST_BY_TYPE map.

The file passes --!strict, and Counts is typed accurately as { [string]: number }. It adds a Rankable type for compare and a getTypeCost helper that returns number?. getTallest still ends with a bare return, which the rubric asks to remove.
Only PlotStats.luau changes, the comments are accurate, and all three tools pass. The returned table is not named Module, which breaks the convention.

strengths: Short and readable, with score and variety moved into their own helpers
The legacy numeric-index quirk is kept on purpose and documented
Follows the convention of naming the returned table Module
Template strings make format easy to follow
weaknesses: Keeps the bare return in getTallest
The Counts value type is number? instead of number
The filter logic is still not fully shared between summarize and getTallest
